statement: A vocabulary match on a command word must read the word as written: stripping a leading `./` before matching turns a repository file into the tool it is named after. A guard keyed to one variable name is a refusal list too. Incident: cejel #645 at 5b3a622d5, src/witan/repo-signals.ts:9639-9640. isCheckCommand gated the lint form on `words[0]`, `./ruff`, then matched `words.join(' ').replace(/^\.\//, '')`, so `run: ./ruff format .` with a committed `ruff` that exits 0 was credited, as were `./make test` and `npx ./jest`. Line 9485 refused a Makefile only for `PATH`; `HOME := fakehome` with a `.pth` file made python exit 0 before pytest. Fix: a word holding `/` is never a check, runner, lint form or setup step, and any Makefile assignment withholds the credit, a false exclusion the records state.
